modules.title: Prepare a car that is ready
Take responsibility for the vehicle and load
Reduce the impact of each journey

curriculum_nodes.title: Your route into driving
curriculum_nodes.objective: Build a personal preparation checklist covering entitlement, permits, supervised practice, risk training and examinations.

curriculum_nodes.title: Am I ready today?
curriculum_nodes.objective: Decide whether to drive in scenarios involving tiredness, illness, medication, alcohol or other drugs, and explain a safer alternative.

curriculum_nodes.title: Pressure is a driving risk
curriculum_nodes.objective: Identify how peers, impulses, confidence and personal circumstances can change a driving decision; rehearse a refusal or alternative.

source_location.heading: ### M01-L03 · Pressure is a driving risk

curriculum_nodes.title: Plan the journey before the ignition
curriculum_nodes.objective: Compare route, departure time, transport mode and passenger choices for safety, accessibility and environmental impact.

source_location.heading: ### M01-L04 · Plan the journey before the ignition

curriculum_nodes.title: Prepare a car that is ready

source_location.heading: ## 2. Prepare a car that is ready

curriculum_nodes.title: Know what the controls tell you
curriculum_nodes.objective: Explain the purpose of core controls, warning indicators, braking and steering systems, and identify when further instructions are needed.

source_location.heading: ### M02-L01 · Know what the controls tell you

curriculum_nodes.title: A check before moving
curriculum_nodes.objective: Organise a safety check of tyres, lights, visibility and vehicle condition, and distinguish a defect from a reason to seek help.

curriculum_nodes.title: Protect everyone inside
curriculum_nodes.objective: Select appropriate restraint arrangements in adult and child passenger scenarios and explain how belts, headrests and airbags work together.

curriculum_nodes.title: Move with control
curriculum_nodes.objective: Plan observation and control for starting, stopping, reversing, hill starts and turning; explain the need for supervised practical practice.

curriculum_nodes.title: Recognise what a sign asks
curriculum_nodes.objective: Classify warning, priority, prohibition, mandatory and instruction signs and describe the decision each category prompts.

source_location.heading: ### M03-L01 · Recognise what a sign asks

curriculum_nodes.title: Combine the instructions
curriculum_nodes.objective: Interpret a sign with a supplementary panel, road marking or signal and identify when a police or guard instruction must be considered.

curriculum_nodes.title: Find your way without rushing
curriculum_nodes.objective: Use direction signs, symbols, facility and service signs to plan a route choice early, including walking and cycling destinations.

source_location.heading: ### M03-L03 · Find your way without rushing

curriculum_nodes.title: Leave room to respond
curriculum_nodes.objective: Explain how observation, speed, reaction time, braking, grip and following space affect the options available in a developing hazard.

curriculum_nodes.title: Decide who goes first
curriculum_nodes.objective: Explain a junction decision using priority signs and right-hand priority, and recognise situations requiring further rule checks.

curriculum_nodes.title: Turn with a complete picture
curriculum_nodes.objective: Plan observation, signalling, position and margins for turns and lane changes, accounting for blind spots and other road users.

source_location.heading: ### M04-L02 · Turn with a complete picture

curriculum_nodes.title: Crossings belong to people
curriculum_nodes.objective: Distinguish pedestrian crossings, cycle passages and cycle crossings and explain the driver's responsibilities in a selected scenario.

curriculum_nodes.title: Choose a safe path through a roundabout
curriculum_nodes.objective: Describe an approach, entry and exit plan that accounts for priority, lanes, signalling and people crossing nearby.

source_location.heading: ### M04-L04 · Choose a safe path through a roundabout

curriculum_nodes.title: See the person behind the movement
curriculum_nodes.objective: Anticipate the needs of children, older people, wheelchair users, cyclists, riders and motorcyclists in street scenarios.

source_location.heading: ### M05-L01 · See the person behind the movement

curriculum_nodes.title: When the street changes purpose
curriculum_nodes.objective: Compare ordinary streets with walking-speed areas, pedestrian streets and cycle streets and choose a suitable driving response.

source_location.heading: ### M05-L02 · When the street changes purpose

curriculum_nodes.title: Choose a lawful place to stop
curriculum_nodes.objective: Distinguish stopping from parking and interpret signs and time panels for a proposed parking place.

source_location.heading: ### M05-L03 · Choose a lawful place to stop

curriculum_nodes.title: Manoeuvre where people may appear
curriculum_nodes.objective: Plan a low-speed parking or reversing manoeuvre with observation, space checks and a decision to stop when the view is insufficient.

source_location.heading: ### M05-L04 · Manoeuvre where people may appear

curriculum_nodes.title: Read the rural road
curriculum_nodes.objective: Identify risks from bends, crests, narrow roads, animals and slow vehicles and justify changes in speed and position.

curriculum_nodes.title: Is passing worth the risk?
curriculum_nodes.objective: Compare staying behind with overtaking in a scenario using visibility, closing speed, space and the ability to abandon the attempt.

source_location.heading: ### M06-L02 · Is passing worth the risk?

curriculum_nodes.title: Join faster traffic calmly
curriculum_nodes.objective: Plan a motorway entry, lane choice, separation and exit, including a safe response to a missed exit.

curriculum_nodes.title: Expect an interrupted route
curriculum_nodes.objective: Interpret railway-crossing and roadworks information and plan a safe approach to changed lanes, queues or a blocked crossing.

curriculum_nodes.title: Drive within what you can see
curriculum_nodes.objective: Choose a visibility and lighting strategy for darkness, fog and glare, considering both seeing and being seen.

source_location.heading: ### M07-L01 · Drive within what you can see

curriculum_nodes.title: Grip is a changing resource
curriculum_nodes.objective: Explain how rain, standing water, ice, snow, tyres and driver inputs can affect stability, steering and braking.

source_location.heading: ### M07-L02 · Grip is a changing resource

curriculum_nodes.title: Protect your attention
curriculum_nodes.objective: Recognise distraction, stress and fatigue in a journey scenario and choose a practical interruption or alternative travel plan.

curriculum_nodes.title: Change the plan when risk grows
curriculum_nodes.objective: Reassess a trip when weather, darkness, delays or passenger pressure accumulate and justify continuing, pausing or cancelling.

source_location.heading: ### M07-L04 · Change the plan when risk grows

curriculum_nodes.title: Take responsibility for the vehicle and load

source_location.heading: ## 8. Take responsibility for the vehicle and load

curriculum_nodes.title: Understand what you may drive
curriculum_nodes.objective: Use entitlement and vehicle-category information to decide what further checks a car or trailer combination requires.

source_location.heading: ### M08-L01 · Understand what you may drive

curriculum_nodes.title: Make the load part of the safety check
curriculum_nodes.objective: Distinguish weight terms, assess a proposed load and identify checks for securing cargo, towing capacity and trailer suitability.

source_location.heading: ### M08-L02 · Make the load part of the safety check

curriculum_nodes.title: Keep the car legally ready
curriculum_nodes.objective: Build an ownership checklist covering registration, insurance, inspection and on-road or off-road status.

source_location.heading: ### M08-L03 · Keep the car legally ready

curriculum_nodes.title: Know what assistance cannot do
curriculum_nodes.objective: Explain why safety systems and different powertrains do not remove the driver's duty to observe, control and recognise limitations.

source_location.heading: ### M08-L04 · Know what assistance cannot do

curriculum_nodes.title: Reduce the impact of each journey

source_location.heading: ## 9. Reduce the impact of each journey

curriculum_nodes.title: Look beyond the exhaust
curriculum_nodes.objective: Compare climate, air-quality and noise effects of travel choices without assuming one vehicle has no environmental impact.

curriculum_nodes.title: Use energy with foresight
curriculum_nodes.objective: Plan smooth, anticipatory driving while preserving safety margins and explain how driving technique can affect energy use.

curriculum_nodes.title: Choose the journey as well as the car
curriculum_nodes.objective: Compare combining trips, walking, cycling, public transport and driving for a realistic personal journey.

source_location.heading: ### M09-L03 · Choose the journey as well as the car

curriculum_nodes.title: Check where the vehicle can go
curriculum_nodes.objective: Find official environmental-zone information and identify what must be checked before entering a restricted area.

source_location.heading: ### M09-L04 · Check where the vehicle can go

curriculum_nodes.title: When the car cannot continue
curriculum_nodes.objective: Compare the response to a breakdown on an ordinary road, a motorway and in a tunnel, explaining how the location changes the priorities.

source_location.heading: ### M10-L01 · When the car cannot continue

curriculum_nodes.title: When someone may be hurt
curriculum_nodes.objective: Identify scene-safety, emergency contact and first-aid learning needs following a collision, and distinguish knowledge from hands-on training.

source_location.heading: ### M10-L02 · When someone may be hurt

curriculum_nodes.title: Explain a whole journey
curriculum_nodes.objective: Review a mixed urban and rural scenario, justify decisions, identify missed hazards and propose safer alternatives.

curriculum_nodes.title: Make a realistic readiness plan
curriculum_nodes.objective: Compare knowledge, practical performance and confidence, then create a plan for further supervised practice and accessible examination preparation.

source_location.heading: ### M10-L04 · Make a realistic readiness plan
